info.title: NetPace
info.description: Cross-platform network speed testing CLI. Measures latency, download and upload speed against Ookla Speedtest servers, with human-readable, CSV and JSON output.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription:
Network speed tester including server discovery, latency measurement, download
and upload speed testing.

commands.name: servers
commands.description: Show the nearest speed test servers.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information.

options.name: --latency
options.description: Include server latency in the results.

options.name: --fastest
options.description:
Show the fastest server details, selected by lowest
latency.
SEE ALSO:
https://github.com/FrankRay78/NetPace/blob/main/USER_GUIDE.md

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information.

options.name: --version
options.description: Prints version information.

options.name: --loop
options.description:
Performs the speed test on
continuous loop.

options.name: --count
options.description:
Stop speed testing after this many
times.

options.name: --delay
options.description:
Time between multiple speed tests
(HH:MM:SS).

options.name: --csv
options.description:
Display output as a single CSV row
(always includes timestamp).
CSV output.

options.name: --csv-delimiter
options.description:
,                Single character delimiter to use in
CSV output.

options.name: --json
options.description: Display output in Json format.

options.name: --json-pretty
options.description:
Display output in Json format
(pretty print).

options.name: --minimal
options.description:
Display the result as a single
compact line.
Ideal for batch scripts and
redirected output.

options.name: --no-latency
options.description:
Do not perform latency test.
When used without --server, the
first available server is selected.

options.name: --no-download
options.description: Do not perform download test.

options.name: --no-upload
options.description: Do not perform upload test.

options.name: --server
options.description:
The url of a specific speed test
sever.
'netpace servers -l' will return
your nearest servers.

options.name: --timestamp
options.description: Include a timestamp in the output.

options.name: --profile
options.description:
Medium           Profile bundle of payload settings
(Tiny | Small | Medium | Large |
Mega).

options.name: --downloadsize
options.description:
Stop the download test after this
many megabytes (IEC MiB).
megabytes (IEC MiB).

options.name: --uploadsize
options.description:
Stop the upload test after this many
megabytes (IEC MiB).

options.name: --unit
options.description:
BitsPerSecond    The speed unit. <BitsPerSecond,
BytesPerSecond>
Applies to the default and minimal
output.

options.name: --unit-scale
options.description:
Auto             The speed unit scale. <Auto, Base,
Kilo, Mega, Giga, Tera, Peta>

options.name: --unit-system
options.description:
SI               The speed unit system. <SI, IEC>
SI steps up in powers of 1000 (KB,
MB, GB), common in networking, while
IEC uses powers of 1024 (KiB, MiB,
GiB), standard in computing and
storage.

options.name: --file
options.description: Write output to file.

options.name: --file-mode
options.description:
Append           Determines file output behavior.
<Append, Overwrite>

options.name: --quiet
options.description:
Suppress all normal console output
(file output still works).

options.name: --fail-on
options.description:
None             Exit with a non-zero code on a
failed measurement. <None, Total,
Partial>
None never affects the exit code;
Total triggers when a test is
all-failed;
Partial triggers on any failed
request. Fail-fast across --count
and --loop.

options.name: --diagnostics
options.description:
Write per-request diagnostic detail
about the run to the error stream.
The result is unchanged, so 'netpace
--json --diagnostics > result.json
2> diagnostics.log' keeps the two
apart.
